picks.title: TimesFM-3: A zero-shot foundation model for multivariate forecasting
picks.excerpt: Google Research released TimesFM-3, a time-series foundation model that forecasts multivariate signals zero-shot, without task-specific training. It targets scientific and operational forecasting workloads from climate to health monitoring.
picks.rationale: A same-day model release that any lab with time-series data can adopt as a zero-shot baseline tomorrow — highest actionability in the pool.

picks.title: IonQ Researchers Run MegaQuOp-Scale Quantum Error Decoder on a MacBook Pro
picks.excerpt: IonQ researchers report decoding simulated MegaQuOp-scale quantum workloads on a consumer MacBook Pro. The result suggests real-time error decoding may not need the dedicated hardware stacks previously assumed.
picks.rationale: If MegaQuOp-scale decoding fits on a laptop, the dedicated-classical-hardware assumption baked into fault-tolerance roadmaps loosens — a concrete, checkable claim, not a roadmap promise.

picks.title: AI searched 100 million possibilities and found a cheaper way to 3D-print a NASA rocket alloy
picks.excerpt: Washington State University researchers used AI to search more than 100 million possible settings for 3D-printing NASA's GRCop-42 alloy. After just 40 experiments the system found six working configurations, one at a record-low 500 watts, opening the alloy to far more common printers.
picks.rationale: Forty physical experiments out of 100 million candidate settings, ending at a record-low 500 W — the clearest number in the pool for how far AI compresses experimental search.

picks.title: New AI method can support real-time management of infectious diseases
picks.excerpt: INRAE researchers applied neural posterior estimation, a deep-learning inference technique, to phylodynamic models of outbreak spread using 72 Ebola genomes. It calibrates epidemiological models far faster and across mixed data types, opening the door to real-time outbreak monitoring.
picks.rationale: Simulation-based inference makes epidemic models fast enough to run during an outbreak instead of after it — a method change with a direct public-health consequence.

picks.title: Generating scenarios for extreme events, without extreme data
picks.excerpt: MIT engineers built a model that predicts plausible extreme events - an extreme storm's likely duration, intensity and footprint - without having seen previous extreme events. It attacks the core data-scarcity problem in climate and risk modeling.
picks.rationale: Generating plausible extreme events with no extreme events in the training data attacks the single hardest constraint in climate and catastrophe-risk modeling.
